title: Hospitality as Christian Witness
definition: Hospitality as Christian Witness is welcoming others in Christ's name so the grace of God becomes visible through practical love.
summary: Hospitality as Christian Witness uses welcome, meals, space, and friendship to display the Gospel to neighbors and strangers.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomed sinners and strangers, and His people reflect His welcome through generous hospitality.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Hospitality as Christian witness is the use of welcome, meals, homes, attention, and presence to display the kindness of Christ. Scripture connects hospitality with love, mission, and care for strangers.

This differs from hospitality inside church life by emphasizing witness to neighbors, unbelievers, and outsiders. It opens ordinary space for Gospel-shaped relationships.

Jesus welcomed people into His presence and ate with sinners without approving sin. Christian hospitality shows His nearness with both grace and truth.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people will not first encounter the Gospel through a sermon, but through a believer who makes room for them. Hospitality as witness turns ordinary life into a doorway for trust, conversation, and mercy.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Invite someone into your life, not only into an event. Share a meal, listen well, ask good questions, and look for natural ways to point to Christ without treating people like projects.
